_about: Pilot English translation of Bedjan p. 1, one entry per punctuation segment (segments.py). Made by Claude (Opus 5.5) from the Kraken OCR on 20-Nov-2026, not checked against Budge's translation (1932) or by a Syriacist. God is addressed with modern You and Your. Words in [ ] are added for sense; {OCR: ...} marks a place where the OCR text is doubtful.
segments: As we call upon the help of the Holy Trinity, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, one {OCR: ܕ for ܚܕ} true God,
we begin to write the book of the Chronography (lit. the writing of the times) {OCR: ܒ̈ܢܐ for ܙܒ̈ܢܐ},
composed by Mar Gregory the Maphrian,
light of the East and of the West,
that is, Abu'l-Faraj son of Aaron the physician, of the city of Melitene {OCR: ܕܝܢܬܐ for ܡܕܝܢܬܐ},
who is called Bar Ebraya (Barhebraeus).
First, a preface.
O God, help my weakness.
Blessed are You, Lord and master of every beginning and every end,
You are the first and You are the last.
Toward You every course [of things] is directed,
and to You every thanksgiving is due;
and to the Son, the Word, the power of Your wisdom,
and to the Holy Spirit, the life of Your being,
from eternity, now and for ever.
And since this rational living being [man] was created to know righteousness, that it may praise it, and goodness, that it may attain it,
and [since] it [gains] the first kind of knowledge from rich theoretical reflections,
and the second from abundant practical teachings (lit. things heard),
the record of the events, good and bad, which took place in every generation
brings no small profit to all those who care to acquire good
and are eager to hate evil;
for it spurs [the reader] to search out the virtues of the former {OCR: ܕܡܢܝܐ, not certain},
and goads [him] to spring away from the vices of the latter.
And when … [continued on p. 2]
notes: Note: other manuscripts: "no small profits" (plural). (1) [variant:] "who care to acquire good and are eager to hate evil".
